records.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher logic inverted: returns false when grant shortcut equals expected value, so it passes for almost any 6-char prefix and test assertions verify nothing
records.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the matcher returns false when the parsed grant shortcut equals the expected shortcut: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Additionally, the grant shortcut is in the last 2 chars of a 6-char context (indexes 4-6), but the code uses `substring(3, 5)`, which is off by one. records.issue_text: Changing form params via setFormParams after Context construction does not refresh derived grantType, which could mislabel the token
records.rationale: In `OAuth2GrantType.Context`, `grantType` is derived once in the constructor (`this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);`). The class still exposes `setFormParams(...)`, but this setter only updates `formParams` and does not recompute `grantType`. Therefore, any code path that constructs `Context` and later calls `setFormParams` (with a different/updated `grant_type`) would leave `context.getGrantType()` stale, and the new logic that propagates it into `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())` could mislabel the token.

records.issue_text: SPI break: new abstract method getShortcut() on OAuth2GrantTypeFactory causes AbstractMethodError for existing third-party factories that don't implement it, breaking token issuance; should be a default method
records.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut();` to the SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (no `default` implementation). In Java, adding a method to an interface is binary-incompatible: any existing third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation compiled against the previous version will not have this method and will fail at runtime when Keycloak calls it (e.g., in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` it unconditionally does `gtf.getShortcut()`). This can manifest as `AbstractMethodError` and break token issuance/boot when such providers are present.
